analysis:
The PR changes documentation only: docs/architecture/model-autopilot.md and docs/provider/cli-reference.md. No executable code, wire protocol, keys, attestation paths or configuration defaults change, so no concrete security regression is identifiable from the supplied evidence. The cli-reference.md base text (unit 1ebf05eb42642970:2) covers only head lines 1-385 of the file. The patch hunks at base lines 1207 and 1287 fall outside it, but their patch text (unit :1) was reviewed directly. Unit :0 is metadata only.

Changes examined:
1. model-autopilot.md line 158 and lines 182-219 document selected-model recovery. After an operation unloads a selected model, recovery reloads it. It may evict an adopted, unheld slot that meets victim rules (min dwell, no per-model lease, idle for the longer of 2 minutes and min_idle_seconds). It may also release an adoption ten minutes after the later of hold expiry and the selected model starting to wait. It never evicts a held slot, the ordinary selection, or an Autopilot pin. This relates to A-018 (serving availability) and TB-012 (add-on hold: recovery pauses during a hold and is cancelled by enterAddonHold). Both are described as source-backed behaviors and carry no unaudited code in this PR. The policy file ProviderLoop+SelectedModelPlacementPolicy.swift is flagged "pending owner review", so the next pass should confirm that the implementation matches these claims.
2. Invariant 10 and the failure-mode bullet on enabled_models restart are documentation of local behavior, with no trust-boundary change.
3. cli-reference.md documents a 15 s per-model unload wait at shutdown, after which native retirement is left to process exit. This is availability and lifecycle behavior with no new attack surface. It touches T-028 (residual GPU memory) only if retirement stalls, and process exit frees the memory.
4. cli-reference.md adds status output text for the restart-needed warning and the Retrying line.

No outstanding cross-file issue was found. Residual question: whether the Swift implementation matches the documented eviction and release rules. That code is outside the supplied evidence.
